'''Lincoln Park''' is an [[urban park]] in [[Jersey City, New Jersey]] with an area of {{convert|273.4|acre|ha|1}}. Part of the [[Hudson County Park System]], it opened in 1905 and was originally known as '''West Side Park'''. The park was designed by Daniel W. Langton and [[Charles N. Lowrie]],<ref name=NJCU>{{cite web | publisher=[[New Jersey City University]] | work=Jersey City: Past and Present | title=Lincoln Park | url=http://www.njcu.edu/programs/jchistory/pages/l_pages/Lincoln_Park.htm | access-date=January 11, 2010 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100204045735/http://www.njcu.edu/programs/jchistory/Pages/L_Pages/Lincoln_Park.htm | archive-date=February 4, 2010 | df=mdy-all }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web   | title = Lincoln Park   | publisher = The Historical Marker Database   | url = http://www.hmdb.org/marker.asp?marker=42419   | access-date = 2011-10-06   | quote = Inscription: Hudson County's great public work of the 1890s was Hudson (now Kennedy) Boulevard, a 20-mile landscaped roadway running through the county. Construction caused the demolition or relocation of many buildings and was completed in 1895. The road marked the Bergen section as the most desirable in Jersey City. Elaborate homes faced the boulevard and side streets. Beginning in 1905 Hudson County's Park Commission began to turn Glendale Woods and the surrounding area, an unsightly swamp, into the 208-acre West Side Park. Under landscape architects Charles Lowrie and Daniel Langton, terraces, ponds, athletic fields, statues, fountains, and flower gardens were built. To create a mall and view of the Orange Mountains a block of buildings were moved from Belmont Avenue. Some were placed on new foundations on Communipaw Avenue. The 1930 statue of Lincoln was sponsored by the Lincoln Association of Jersey City (1865), the oldest group of its kind in the nation. The park contains a lake, a classic fountain (restored in 2016), pavilions, and memorials to Jersey City's Union Civil War veterans and firemen. Nearby are prime residential streets of Gifford and Bentley Avenues, the 1925 Temple Beth-El and the 1909 Saint Aloysius Church, a 900 seat French Renaissance edifice. Its 150 foot bell tower has been a landmark for generations.   | archive-date = October 20, 2011   | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20111020053149/http://www.hmdb.org/marker.asp?marker=42419   | url-status = dead   }}</ref> both founding members of the [[American Society of Landscape Architects]] and part of the [[City Beautiful movement]].

The park consists of two distinct sections: Lincoln Park East, {{convert|150.4|acre|ha}}, and Lincoln Park West, {{convert|123|acre|ha}}.<ref name=HCPMP/> The sections are named for their positions relative to [[U.S. Route 1/9 Truck]], which passes between them, and are connected by foot and vehicular bridges over the highway. The Lincoln Park Nature Walk is part of [[wetlands]] restoration project adjacent to the [[Hackensack River]]. The [[Hackensack RiverWalk]] is a partially completed [[greenway (landscape)|greenway]] along the banks of the river running the length of the [[Hudson County]] shoreline. The [[East Coast Greenway]] also traverses the park.<ref>[http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2012/06/new_bike_path_connects_jersey.html New Bike Path Connects Jersey] By Daniel Reyes/The Jersey Journal, 25 June 2012</ref>

==History==
Lincoln Park was the first park in the [[Hudson County, New Jersey|Hudson County]] parks system. The Hudson County Parks Commission was created in 1903, and began work on the park in 1904. The park was built primarily on undeveloped swamp and the privately owned Glendale Woods.<ref>{{cite book | title=Jersey City | last=Shaloub | first=Patrick B. | page=90 | year=1995 | publisher=Arcadia Publishing | isbn=9780752402550 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GUWQLmEIGUwC&q=%22west+side+park%22+%22jersey+city%22&pg=PA90}}</ref> By 1925, {{convert|85|acre|ha}} of land had been reclaimed from the Hackensack River in the western portion of the park.<ref name=NYTGolf>{{cite news|title=Golfers to Have $1,000,000 Course|newspaper=The New York Times|date=June 22, 1925}}</ref> The park was expanded again in 1938 with the acquisition of additional properties along the [[Hackensack River]].<ref>{{cite news | work=The New York Times | date=January 8, 1938 | page=28 | title=Land Deals Extend Jersey City Park; Hudson Commission Buys Nine Parcels on River Front and Communipaw Avenue}}</ref> The Lincoln Park Nature Walk is part of {{convert|31|acre|m2|adj=on}} [[wetlands]] restoration project on a former landfill site adjacent to the [[Hackensack River]] unveiled in July 2011. It is hoped that the nearly $10.6 million development will enhance bird and fish populations.<ref name = restored>{{Cite web   | last = Whiten   | first = Jon   | title = Restored Wetlands Area in Lincoln Park Now Open to the Public   | publisher = Jersey City Independent   | date = Jul 19, 2011   | url = http://www.jerseycityindependent.com/2011/07/19/restored-wetland-area-in-lincoln-park-now-open-to-the-public/   | access-date = 2011-07-21   | archive-date = July 26, 2011   | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110726114355/http://www.jerseycityindependent.com/2011/07/19/restored-wetland-area-in-lincoln-park-now-open-to-the-public/   | url-status = dead   }}</ref> A section of the [[East Coast Greenway]] crosses through the park,<ref>{{cite web   | title = Welcome to the East Coast Greenway in New Jersey   | work = East Coast Greenway   | url = http://www.greenway.org/nj.aspx   | access-date = 2011-07-05   | archive-date = September 27, 2011   | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110927035332/http://www.greenway.org/nj.aspx | url-status = dead }}</ref> which is site of one of five kiosks in the state for the project<ref>{{Citation   | last = Copeland   | first = Denise (Betty the Bike)   | title = Weekend kiosk building party at Lincoln Park, Jersey City, for the East Coast Greenway   | newspaper = The Jersey Journal   | date = December 9, 2010   | url = http://blog.nj.com/nj_off-road_biking/2010/12/ecg_kiosk_jersey_city.html   | access-date = 2011-09-28   }}</ref>

A [[West Side Park (Jersey City baseball)|ballpark]] within the grounds was the home of the [[Jersey City Skeeters]] of the [[Eastern League (1916)|Eastern League]] from 1902 through 1905.

==Facilities==
[[File:Pulaski Skyway fr Lincoln Pk jeh.JPG|thumb|Three of the baseball fields, with [[Pulaski Skyway]] and smokestacks of the [[Kearny Generating Station]] in background]]
[[File:Lincoln Pk ECGW ribbon cutting jeh.jpg|thumb|Ceremonial opening of [[East Coast Greenway]] segment in the park]]

===Athletics and recreation===

Lincoln Park East contains many sports fields and recreational facilities. There are 21 outdoor [[tennis court]]s, seven baseball fields, a cricket pitch, three children's playgrounds, the [[Charlie Mays]] running track, five basketball courts, two football fields, two soccer fields, and four handball/paddleball courts.<ref name=HCPMP>{{cite web|title=Hudson County Park Master Plan|url=http://njedl.rutgers.edu/ftp/PDFs/992.pdf|publisher=T&M Associates|access-date=May 11, 2011|pages=2–18|date=November 1998|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725183021/http://njedl.rutgers.edu/ftp/PDFs/992.pdf|archive-date=July 25, 2011|df=mdy-all}}</ref> This section of the park also contains a {{convert|3|acre|ha}} lake available for fishing.<ref>{{cite web|title=Places to Fish - Ponds, Lakes and Rservoirs|url=http://www.state.nj.us/dep/fgw/fishplc.htm|work=www.state.nj.us|publisher=New Jersey Division of Fish & Wildlife|access-date=May 11, 2011}}</ref> The lake has also been used for [[Model yachting|model yacht]] racing.<ref>{{cite news|title=MODEL YACHTS COMPETE; Millpond Club of Jersey Wins Regatta in Jersey City|newspaper=The New York Times|date=May 31, 1937|page=32}}</ref> In 2009, a suspected virus resulted in a large number of [[carp]] dying in the lake.<ref>{{cite news|last=Takahash|first=Paul|title=Viruses may be killing Lincoln Park carp|url=http://www.nj.com/news/jjournal/jerseycity/index.ssf?/base/news-8/1249021523137500.xml&coll=3|access-date=May 11, 2011|newspaper=The Jersey Journal|date=July 31, 2009|archive-date=January 23, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110123182304/http://www.nj.com/news/jjournal/jerseycity/index.ssf?/base/news-8/1249021523137500.xml&coll=3|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Lincoln Park West features [[wetlands]] with hiking trails and Joseph J. Jaroschak Field, the facility for the baseball, softball, and men's and women's [[soccer]] teams of [[Saint Peter's University]]. The field was opened and dedicated in 1990 by Mary Lou Jaroschak, and named after her late husband.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://saintpeterspeacocks.com/facilities/joseph-j-jaroschak-field/1|title=Joseph J. Jaroschak Field|publisher=Saint Peter's University|access-date=March 25, 2024}}</ref> 

In 2011, construction began on a nine-hole public golf course in Lincoln Park West, the first public course in Hudson County.<ref>{{cite news|last=Wilshe|first=Brett|title=Hudson County freeholders approve building county's first public golf course adjacent to Lincoln Park in Jersey City|newspaper=The Jersey Journal|date=December 11, 2010}}</ref> Skyway Golf Course, named after the [[Pulaski Skyway]], opened in May 2015 after environmental restoration, grading, and landscaping.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2015/05/hudson_county_golf_course_to_open_next_month.html|title=Fore! Hudson County golf course to open next month in Jersey City|date=May 2015|website=NJ.com|access-date=October 1, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2015/06/hudson_countys_first_public_golf_course_to_open_mo.html|title=Tee time: Hudson County's first public golf course set to open Monday|date=June 2015|website=NJ.com|access-date=October 1, 2017}}</ref> Previously, the golf course was the location of a [[batting cages]] and a [[driving range]].

[[New York Road Runners]] hosts a weekly 2.7-mile Open Run.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lincoln Park=NYRR|date=2023-08-23|last=Staff|first=NYRR|url=https://www.nyrr.org/openrun/parks/lincoln-park|access-date=2023-08-23}}</ref>

===Structures and buildings===
Lincoln Park East has four [[gazebo]]s, several maintenance buildings, and the Park Administration Building.<ref name=HCPMP/> The Administration Building houses offices as well as the Hank Gallo Community Room.

===Casino in the Park===
Just south of the Lincoln Park Lake is Casino in the Park, a catering facility owned by the county and leased to a private operator. The original structure was built as a clubhouse for the tennis courts, but was underutilized due to the distance between them.<ref name=NJCU/> It was used as a summer museum by the Jersey City Public Library before being leased to Ray Dillman, manager of the [[El Morocco]] nightclub in New York City, as a restaurant.

The restaurant is regularly used for meetings and events. Many well known people have attended private and public events at the venue. In 1963, [[Frank Sinatra]] attended his parents' 50th wedding anniversary celebration at Casino in the Park alongside his daughter and [[Rat Pack|Rat Pack "Clan"]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Sinatra Attends As Parents Note Golden Wedding|newspaper=Hartford Courant|date=Feb 10, 1963|page=8B}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Journal|first=John Gomez/For The Jersey|date=2019-04-29|title=Hold that wrecking ball! Historian issues plea to save N.J. landmark {{!}} Legends & Landmarks|url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2019/04/hold-that-wrecking-ball-historian-issues-plea-to-save-nj-landmark-legends-landmarks.html|access-date=2022-02-20|website=nj|language=en}}</ref> In 1991, the Hudson County Democratic Organization was addressed by then Arkansas Governor [[Bill Clinton]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Mighty HCDO has fallen: No dinner, just breakfast|url=http://www.nj.com/columns/jjournal/index.ssf?/base/columns-0/125455116237780.xml&coll=3|access-date=May 18, 2011|newspaper=The Jersey Journal|date=October 3, 2009|archive-date=October 16, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121016061037/http://www.nj.com/columns/jjournal/index.ssf?/base/columns-0/125455116237780.xml&coll=3|url-status=dead}}</ref> It was also the location of weekly meetings of the [[Rotary Club]] of Jersey City.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Rotary Club of Jersey City, New Jersey USA|url=http://www.jc-rotary.org|work=www.jc-rotary.org|access-date=May 19, 2011}}</ref>

The city leases the building to a private enterprise.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2019/04/owners-of-two-downtown-jersey-city-restaurants-want-to-run-new-casino-in-the-park.html|title=Owners of two Downtown Jersey City restaurants want to run new Casino in the Park|date=April 23, 2019}}</ref>

The original building was demolished in April 2020 and a replacement called "The View at Lincoln Park" is set to be completed in September 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2019/10/heres-a-look-at-the-venue-that-will-replace-jersey-citys-iconic-casino-in-the-park.html|title = Here's a look at the venue replacing Jersey City's iconic Casino in the Park|date = October 3, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Ulloa|first=Daniel|date=2021-02-03|title=Jersey City Planning Board approves new design to replace historic Casino in the Park|url=https://hudsoncountyview.com/jersey-city-planning-board-approves-new-design-to-replace-historic-casino-in-the-park/|access-date=2022-02-20|website=Hudson County View|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Staff|first=Jersey City Times|date=2021-05-18|title=County Breaks Ground on "The View at Lincoln Park"|url=https://jcitytimes.com/county-breaks-ground-on-the-view-at-lincoln-park/|access-date=2022-02-20|website=Jersey City Times|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Former facilities==
 
[[West Side Park (Jersey City baseball)|Skeeters Park]] was a minor league baseball field with bleachers and a grandstand with a seating capacity of 8,500 people, built in 1902.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Weiss|first1=Bill|last2=Wright|first2=Marshall|title=Jersey City Skeeters|url=http://web.minorleaguebaseball.com/milb/history/top100.jsp?idx=7|work=100 Best Minor League Baseball Teams|publisher=MLB.com|access-date=June 9, 2011|archive-date=November 4, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101104034354/http://web.minorleaguebaseball.com/milb/history/top100.jsp?idx=7|url-status=dead}}</ref> It was home to the [[Jersey City Skeeters]], a minor league baseball team from 1902 to 1905.

A nine-hole golf course was built on {{convert|140|acre|ha}} of the western portion of the park in 1925.<ref name="NYTGolf"/> The park also had a concrete swimming pool {{convert|40|by|130|ft|m|sp=us}} near the athletic fields.<ref name="NYTGolf"/>

==Art==
[[File:Lincoln the Mystic-4.jpg|thumb|upright|left| ''Lincoln the Mystic'' at eastern entrance]]
[[File:Lincoln Park fountain jeh.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Lincoln Park Fountain]]
The primary piece of [[public art]] in the park is ''[[Lincoln the Mystic]]'', a statue by [[James Earle Fraser (sculptor)|James Earle Fraser]] commissioned in 1929<ref>{{cite news | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=January 24, 1999 | last=James | first=George | title=For 134 Years, Jersey City Puts Politics Aside and Honors Lincoln | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/01/24/nyregion/jerseyana-for-134-years-jersey-city-puts-politics-aside-and-honors-lincoln.html | access-date=January 11, 2010}}</ref> by the Lincoln Association of Jersey City.<ref>{{Cite web   | last = Karnoutsos   | first = Carmela    |author2=Patrick Shalhoub  | title = Abraham Lincoln Association of Jersey City   | work = Jersey City Past and Present | publisher = New Jersey City University | year = 2009 | url = http://www.njcu.edu/programs/jchistory/Pages/L_Pages/Lincoln_Association_of_Jersey_City.htm   | access-date = November 9, 2011}}</ref> The sculpture was dedicated on June 14, 1930.<ref>{{cite news | title=New Lincoln Monument Is Unveiled Today | work=The Jersey Journal | date=June 14, 1930}}</ref> 4,000 people attended the unveiling and the crowd was addressed by New Jersey Governor [[Morgan F. Larson]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jersey City Unveils Monument of Lincoln|newspaper=The New York Times|date=June 15, 1930}}</ref>

The park is also home to the world's largest concrete monument, the 365-ton Lincoln Park Fountain designed by Pierre J. Cheron at the center of the park's traffic circle.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Scheller|first1=William G.|last2=Scheller|first2=Kay|title=New Jersey:A Guide to Unique Places|year=2006|publisher=Globe Pequot|isbn=978-0-7627-4055-0|page=28}}</ref> The fountain is {{convert|53|ft|m|sp=us}} tall, and contains 27 frog-shaped spouts and 150 lights.<ref>{{cite news|work=The Cement Age|date=May 1912|title=An Artistic Concrete Fountain|last=Collins|first=A.B.|page=257}}</ref><ref>{{citation | last = Hack   | first = Charles   | title = Hudson County freeholders approve spending $3.9M on restoring Lincoln Park's 100-year-old fountain | newspaper = The Jersey Journal | date = June 9, 2012 | url = http://www.nj.com/jjournal-news/index.ssf/2012/06/hudson_county_freeholders_appr_1.html   | access-date = June 9, 2012 }}</ref> The fountain was rededicated on June 16, 2016, after a $7.2 million restoration.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nj.com/jjournal-news/index.ssf/2016/06/jersey_citys_lincoln_park_foun.html|title=Jersey City's Lincoln Park Fountain is lit in rededication ceremony|author= Nicholas Zeitlinger|date=June 18, 2016|website=NJ.com|access-date=December 27, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2021/06/hudson-county-sues-architect-behind-historic-lincoln-park-fountain-renovation.html|title = Hudson County sues architect behind historic Lincoln Park Fountain renovation|date = June 21, 2021}}</ref>

The park also contains several monuments and memorials:
[[File:Civil war statue LP jeh.jpg|thumb|right|Civil War memorial]]
* The Jersey City [[American Civil War|Civil War]] Memorial was dedicated on May 28, 1926. The bronze sculpture is {{convert|9|ft|m|sp=us}} tall and depicts a marching Civil War soldier dressed in a full uniform. Originally intended to be placed in Hamilton Park, the memorial was installed by the executor of the estate of Edward J. Donnelly, Sergeant, Company C, [[5th New Jersey Volunteer Infantry]].<ref>{{cite news|title=War Memorial Legacy Upheld|url=https://timesmachine.nytimes.com/timesmachine/1922/11/04/99095349.pdf|access-date=May 10, 2011|newspaper=The New York Times|date=November 4, 1922}}</ref>
[[File:Fireman monument Lincoln Pk JC jeh.jpg|thumb|right|Detail of the Farrier Memorial]]
* The Farrier Memorial, a {{convert|6|ft|m|sp=us|adj=on}} bronze statue of a firefighter atop a domed granite base of {{convert|15|ft|m|sp=us}}, was a bequest by Police Captain Frederick T. Farrier to honor the Volunteer Fire Department and was dedicated on November 21, 1931.<ref>{{Cite web   | title = Farrier Memorial | publisher = The Historical Marker Database    | url = http://www.hmdb.org/Marker.asp?Marker=42413 | access-date = 2011-10-06}}</ref>
* The [[Great Famine (Ireland)|Great Irish Famine]] Memorial, erected by the Friendly Sons of St. Patrick, is a [[Celtic cross]] of {{convert|18|ft|m|sp=us}} and was dedicated on May 8, 2011.<ref>{{cite news|last=Mestanza|first=Jean-Pierre|title=100 in Lincoln Park welcome new memorial to Great Irish Famine|url=http://www.nj.com/news/jjournal/jerseycity/index.ssf?/base/news-12/1304923210321110.xml&coll=3|access-date=May 10, 2011|newspaper=The Jersey Journal|date=May 9, 2011|archive-date=October 16, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121016012125/http://www.nj.com/news/jjournal/jerseycity/index.ssf?/base/news-12/1304923210321110.xml&coll=3|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== In popular culture ==

* In the [[The Sopranos (The Sopranos episode)|pilot episode]] of the [[HBO]] crime drama ''[[The Sopranos]]'', the former driving range at Lincoln Park West, near the [[Pulaski Skyway]], featured in a scene.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sopranos-locations.com/locations/golf-course-(pilot)/|title=The Sopranos location guide - Golf course (Pilot)|last=Ugoku|website=www.sopranos-locations.com|language=en|access-date=2020-03-04}}</ref>

Lincoln park is also featured in the HBO miniseries The Plot Against America where actor Johnathon Tuturo can be seen riding a horse by the fountain circle
